page: Microsoft Azure F16ams_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine configuration within the compute-optimized family, tailored with an elevated memory allocation. It provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The hardware features a 1-to-1 thread-to-core configuration, eliminating hyperthreading contention. Cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. Supported vector and instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration through AES, VAES, and SHA extensions.

Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations show strong memory throughput, registering a PassMark memory score of 2777.71, which ranks in the top 25 percent. In compute benchmarks, the AMD EPYC cores deliver strong single-core performance with a stress-ng score of 3078.78, while multi-threaded decompression in bzip3 reaches 200.28 GB/sec. Small language model inference exhibits high execution rates, processing 3006.69 prompt tokens per second and generating 342.9 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model. Sustained multi-core stress testing and standard PassMark CPU benchmarks align within the median performance tiers.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated graphics processing units, relying entirely on remote premium storage attachments for data persistence. Network configurations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The hardware balance makes the F16ams_v6 cost-effective for workloads requiring high RAM capacity per core without necessitating high GPU acceleration or ephemeral local disks. Appropriate workloads include in-memory caching systems, Redis clusters, relational and analytical database nodes, mid-tier data transformation pipelines, and parallel batch processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure F16ams_v6 is a virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 physical cores operating at 3.7 GHz, paired with 128.0 GB of memory. It offers an 8.0 GB per-core allocation without hyperthreading, supported by AVX-512 vector instruction extensions. Benchmark results highlight strong single-core execution with a stress-ng score of 3078.78 and high-tier small language model text generation exceeding 342 tokens per second. Memory throughput places in the upper quartile, supporting up to 75.42 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. The instance includes no bundled local storage and no GPUs, utilizing network-attached premium storage instead. It is well suited for memory-intensive batch processing, in-memory databases, and continuous data aggregation tasks.
